$comment: #259. `packages/ui` and the three scripts that audit it are excluded HERE rather than simply un-listed,
and the reason is a measured behaviour of tsc, not tidiness: TypeScript follows imports out of an
`exclude`d directory. This program is the one that makes a stray `document` in packages/contracts or
apps/control-plane a COMPILE error: `lib` is `["ES2023"]`, `types` is `["node"]`, there is no `DOM` and no
`jsx`. `scripts/check-ui.ts` imports packages/ui modules, so leaving it here would drag every `.tsx`
screen into a program that has no `jsx` and fail with TS6142 (measured), and the tempting fix -- adding
`jsx` and `DOM` to this file -- is the trade this issue refuses to make. So the UI tree, and the gate
scripts that read it, are checked by packages/ui/tsconfig.json instead, which owns `jsx` and `DOM`.
That exclusion is only safe if nothing escapes checking. scripts/check-project.ts enforces it: the union
of every `typecheck` project's include list must equal the `.ts`/`.tsx` set on disk, in both directions --
a file in no program is unchecked (fails), a file in two programs is two sets of lib/jsx answers for one file
(fails). So neither a UI source nor a stray `.tsx` can become invisible by editing this list.
Adding a screen-bearing app later (the UI-OD1 shell under apps/) is legal and is NOT forbidden by
accident: give that app its own tsconfig.json with `jsx`, add one explicit
`tsc --noEmit -p apps/<name>` invocation to the `typecheck` script, and the coverage gate does the rest.
It is not done here because the shell's shape is the maintainer's open decision, not this change's.
